As of 400 AM EST Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Confidence remains very high regarding an impactful 
storm across the region from later today into Thanksgiving Day with 
heavy rainfall and strong to potentially damaging winds.

The pieces are starting to come together for a developing low 
pressure system to strengthen and lift northward near or over the 
area tonight into Thanksgiving. 1040mb high pressure has moved into 
New England with an inverted ridge extending southward to the east 
of the Appalachians. Broad low pressure is taking shape near and 
south of FL early this morning. Phasing of northern and southern 
stream upper troughs will commence this afternoon into the evening, 
resulting in rapid deepening of the surface low as it lifts 
northward off the Carolina coast tonight. The consensus of the 00z 
guidance suite results in even more cause for concern as most models 
now show the low deepening to around 995mb with high pressure over 
New England building as high as 1044mb. 00z models have also finally 
converged on a low track with low pressure lifting N and then 
turning NW into central NC and VA Wednesday night into Thursday as 
the upper troughs phase into a negatively tilted configuration. Rain 
spreads northward to the I-64 corridor and points south by mid 
afternoon and into the remainder of the area by this evening. The 
greatest impacts are expected from midnight tonight into the early 
afternoon on Thanksgiving. The low moves into/across the region 
Thursday afternoon with decreasing winds and precip. With a farther 
west low track, a larger portion of the area will get into the warm 
sector of the system. Instability will be limited but with the 
extreme kinematic fields some thunder is possible. If more than 
meager instability is able to materialize, a severe/tornado threat 
may also be of concern Thursday morning. SPC does not currently have 
any of the area outlooked but trends will be followed closely over 
the next 24 hours given the extreme wind shear aloft. 

With ~50mb of differential between low and high pressure, very 
strong to locally damaging winds are increasingly likely along 
the Atlantic coast and western shore of the Chesapeake Bay. High
Wind Warnings have been expanded to include Newport News and 
points northward along the western shore of the bay. This is in 
addition to the entire Eastern Shore and Portsmouth, Norfolk, VA
Beach, and Currituck County in NC. Tree damage and power 
outages are a distinct possibility in these area with gusts 
55-65+ mph during the peak of the storm late tonight into 
Thursday. Locations along the immediate Atlantic coast may gust 
up to 70 mph. A Wind Advisory has been issued for the remainder 
of the area not included in the High Wind Warning. Gusts of 
35-45 mph are forecast in the Piedmont with 40-50 mph gusts 
expected along and east of I-95. Some tree damage and power 
outages are also possible in the Wind Advisory area, especially 
east of 95. 

The potential for widespread heavy rainfall has increased in the 00z 
guidance as well. Area average rainfall has increased to 2-3" over 
the western half of the area with 3-5" to the east. A Flood Watch 
has been issued for areas along and east of a line from Brunswick 
County VA north and east into the Tri-Cities, Richmond Metro, 
Northern Neck, and MD Eastern Shore. Despite the very dry
antecedent conditions, much of this rain will fall in a 6-12 
hour period late tonight into early Thursday. Flash flooding is 
most likely in urban and poor drainage areas, especially with 
any remaining leaves coming down in the coincident strong winds 
and clogging drainage systems. Some of the recent hi-res 
guidance suggests higher rainfall totals may be realized across 
the Piedmont as well, so some westward or northwestward 
adjustments to the Flood Watch are possible.
 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Significant coastal flooding is expected Thursday 
into Friday, with widespread major flooding and potentially near-
record water levels at a few locations. 

Confidence is high in a significant coastal flooding event Thursday 
into Friday as a strengthening coastal low tracks inland across the 
Mid-Atlantic while strong high pressure remains anchored over New 
England. The combination of prolonged strong E-NE winds, an 
exceptionally tight pressure gradient, and elevated astronomical 
tides associated with the ongoing King Tide cycle will result in 
substantial tidal departures across the Chesapeake, tidal rivers, and 
Atlantic coast.

Coastal Flood Warnings are now in effect for all threatened portions 
of the tidal forecast area, including the upper James River adjacent 
to Hopewell/Jordan Point, which was added with this issuance. The 
remaining Coastal Flood Watches have also been upgraded to warnings 
as confidence continues to increase in widespread major coastal 
flooding. The most significant impacts are still expected with the
